subject: Holdline renewal: bridge package request and SLA overlay — exec concurrence needed
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@holdline.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal concerns — need a bridge to re-sign

Hi Michael / Marissa,

Quick context: our renewal quote arrived with a ~22% list increase driven by model licensing bands and minimum committed throughput. Given current usage and our upcoming product roadmap we can't absorb that jump this quarter.

We value Redwood’s runtime but need a path to keep the product in production while we finalize an internal budget reallocation. Specific asks from procurement:
- A short-term term reset (extend current pricing for 6 months)
- A one-time credit to offset the immediate delta (~15–20% of ARR)
- An SLA overlay (higher uptime SLA for two quarters) or a guarantee that critical incidents will get priority escalation + a service credit if missed

Can you outline what concessions Redwood can offer and any exec approval required? We’d like a definitive answer this week to present to finance.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Patel
Head of Procurement — Holdline, Inc.

Key items from procurement: term reset 6 months, one-time credit (15–20% ARR), SLA overlay + faster escalation. I attached their MRR breakdown for numbers (see attachment).

Can Dev and Marissa weigh in on margin impact and what level of approval we need to proceed? If this requires exec signoff, please call it out and I’ll escalate.

Thanks — Michael

Thanks for the context, Michael. I reviewed the attached MRR sheet and ran the concession math. Quick summary:

- Current ARR: ~$420,000
- Proposed list adjustment: +22% (immediate impact)
- Procurement asks equate to ~15–20% ARR relief in year 1; call it a $63k–$84k effective concession

Recommendation (business + risk balanced):
1) One-time make-good credit equal to 15% of current ARR ($63k) applied on renewal invoice.
2) Term reset: preserve current pricing/tiers for 6 months (no relicensing in that period).
3) SLA overlay: commit to a 99.9% uptime SLA for next two quarters with a capped credit policy (max 25% of monthly charges per incident, cumulative cap to be defined) and priority incident routing.

Impact and notes:
- Net margin hit ~12–14% in year 1 after credits (acceptable given strategic nature).
- Risk: sets precedent — include language limiting this to one-time bridge and tied to mutual action plan (MAP) milestones.
- Legal will need to approve amendment language and credit calculations.

If you want to proceed I think this requires Laura's concurrence (executive approval) because of the ARR-level concession + SLA commitment. I attached a draft amendment (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf) for legal redline prep.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_amendment_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting exec concurrence: Holdline bridge package (details + language)

Laura — looping you in for sign-off. Below is the concrete package we recommend and the language to include in the amendment. The customer will move to sign DocuSign immediately if we can commit.

Recommended concession package (for executive approval):
- One-time credit: 15% of ARR applied to first renewal invoice (approx. $63,000).
- Term reset: extend existing pricing tiers for 6 months from renewal effective date.
- SLA overlay: 99.9% uptime commitment for two quarters following renewal; service credit triggers per incident with a cumulative cap equal to 25% of monthly charges.
- Condition: This is a one-time bridge only, valid if Holdline signs the attached MAP and agrees to an onboarding plan with checkpoints in 30/60/90 days.

Suggested amendment clause (short form):
"Redwood agrees to provide a one-time credit equal to 15% of the Customer's annual recurring revenue as of the renewal effective date, to be credited on the invoice following execution of this Amendment. Redwood will maintain Customer's existing pricing tiers for a six (6) month period from the renewal effective date. For a period of six (6) months following renewal Redwood will implement a 99.9% uptime SLA for the Services listed in Exhibit A. Service credits and cumulative caps are defined in Exhibit B. This concession is a one-time accommodation and void if Customer fails to comply with the MAP attached as Schedule 1."

Links: HubSpot deal + DocuSign prepared here — https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7834 and https://www.docusign.com/containers/ABC-7834-amendment

Can you confirm approval (or provide edits) by EOD so I can send the DocuSign?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting exec concurrence: Holdline bridge package (details + language)

Approved with conditions.

Laura's decision (summary):
- Approve the one-time credit at 15% ARR ($63k).
- Approve the six-month term reset on the condition the MAP milestones are unambiguous and signed.
- Approve SLA overlay but cap exposure: per-incident credit up to 25% of monthly charges, and an aggregate maximum credit across the six-month SLA period equal to 50% of two months' average charges (legal to draft Exhibit B).

Operational asks before sending DocuSign:
1) Legal to draft exhibits and finalize cumulative credit cap language.
2) CS to build the MAP with concrete 30/60/90 deliverables and acceptance criteria.
3) Sales Ops to confirm how credit will be invoiced and reflected in AR.

Marissa/Dev — proceed to send DocuSign with the draft amendment and include the MAP as Schedule 1. Tag Legal and CS for immediate review. Notify me once DocuSign is sent.

— Laura Bennett
VP, Global Sales | Redwood Inference
